plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Trim CRWD to 10% to further reduce single name risk.
Add QQQI to 15% to increase income-generating assets.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and lower volatility.
Expect a lower target return with significantly reduced drawdown potential.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns with a focus on capital preservation. Expect a target monthly return around 1.5%, with significantly reduced risk of large drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to low single digits.
Maintain modest exposure to MUU and METU.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and increase cash buffer.
Trim CRWD to 8% to manage single name risk.
Add QQQI to 10% for a blend of growth and income.
This plan balances risk reduction with continued growth potential.
balanced.read: This balanced strategy seeks risk-first growth, aiming for approximately 2.5% monthly returns. It reduces concentration and leverage while maintaining exposure to quality tech and income assets, with a moderate buffer against downturns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to 6% each.
Maintain SPY at 25% for broad market exposure.
Increase CRWD to 15% to concentrate on a top performer.
Add TSLA as a new position at 5% from the scanner.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly increased drawdown risk and volatility.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan aims for higher returns (target ~4%/mo) by increasing leverage and concentrating on high-scoring setups. Be aware that this significantly raises potential drawdowns and is subject to leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, CRWD, SNOW).
Increase QQQI to 40% to maximize income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce overall portfolio volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and capital preservation.
Expect lower growth but a more stable portfolio with reliable distributions.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income-focused plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and capital preservation, targeting around 1% monthly. It significantly reduces volatility and risk by cutting leverage and growth stocks, focusing on income ETFs and a reduced broad index allocation.
